newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JULY 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JULY 8.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The Cabinet will meet exclusively on the fate of inflation on Thursday, to discuss probable pressure on anti-inflationary policies through to the end of the year. Estimates now put the rate of inflation by the end of the year at 4.8-5.0 percent.

--The new framework of operations for foreign exchange deposits will be revealed within the week. Forex deposits have been completely deregulated, Bank of Greece governor Lucas Papademos says, because pressure has been contained and the conditions are right.

--The floating of the Public Electricity Corporation (DEH) on the stock exchange will form a major part of a forthcoming bill on the deregulation of the energy market, with final touches to plans being put soon.

--A scaling back of subsidies is the major characteristic of investments approved for first half year 1997, marking a clear change in development philosophy. Some 87.8 billion drachmas in subsidies from a total 210.1 billion drachmas for 916 investment plans has been approved.

--Employers will be liable for a fine of up to 500,000 drachmas for each uninsured employee, in accordance with a new bill to combat the lack of payment of contributions to the Social Security Foundation IKA, Labour and Social Security Minister Miltiades Papaioannou said yesterday. IKA will be able to claim payment from debtors which will involve the lifting of bank confidentiality and a new team of auditors will be established to conduct checks on firms.
--The bill on how IKA plans to recoup the 620 billion drachmas owed to it will be submitted to Parliament by the end of August.
--The fall in interest rates has prompted the Bank of Greece to consider allowing banks to refinance mortgages and housing loans.
--The collection of revenues from the new tax on large real estate holdings has been unaccountably delayed, due to foot-dragging on the selection of a firm to process the forms.

--The Greek diary market is ploughing its money into the development of new cheese products, according to a new sector study by ICAP. The products, mainly feta, are exported to the European Union, the US, the Americans and Saudi Arabia.

--US IRA experts have assisted the finance ministry in developing a new tax collection system, which is currently being implemented as part of a pilot programme in selected tax bureaux around Athens and the countryside. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
